FOR campaign/the-murrain -- THE SELF-ANCHORING FIX IS THE RIGHT SHAPE AND IT INTRODUCED TWO DEFECTS, ONE OF WHICH I SET YOU UP FOR. 39d7fb7331f7. Three things, ordered by how much they matter.

1. THE PRECONDITION ASSERT IS NOW A TAUTOLOGY. This is my fault as much as yours -- I suggested a search that "asserts it found one" and did not say the old assert had to go with it.

     .find_map(|rows| { let living = ...; (living.len() == 2).then_some(living) })
     .expect("seed 1 retains a measured shared column");
   assert_eq!(colocated.len(), 2, "fixture precondition: two living rung occupants share this column");

   The closure only yields Some when living.len() == 2, so colocated has length 2 by construction and that assert cannot fail. It was load-bearing when the vertex was hard-coded -- it checked the fixture still held two living occupants -- and the search absorbed its job. Delete it, or it is a green line that looks like a check. This repo has a name for the shape: the precondition doing the work instead of the claim.

2. THE SEARCH IS WEAKER THAN THE PROPERTY THE TEST DOCUMENTS, and this is the one I would actually fix. The doc comment says:

     "a surface and subterranean community may intentionally share one player
      address; both the room's name and its occupation use the first settlement"

   The search takes the FIRST column with two living occupants. It does not require one surface and one subterranean. Two surface settlements sharing a vertex would satisfy it, and then the regression this test exists for -- the surface/subterranean case -- is no longer exercised while the test stays green. The hard-coded 2103 at least had that property measured into it. Add the discriminating condition to the search: find a column whose two living occupants are one surface and one subterranean, and let the expect() fail loudly if no such column exists. That keeps the robustness AND the meaning.

3. THE SEED CHANGED 42 -> 1 AND THE COMMIT DOES NOT SAY SO. "test(the-murrain): refresh shared-room regression fixture" does not mention it. Two reasons it deserves a sentence:

   - Seed 42 is this repo's canonical seed -- fixtures, galleries, almanacs, the byte-identity guards. Moving a regression test off it is a real change, not a refresh.
   - More interesting: if you switched because seed 42 no longer HAS a column with two living co-located occupants, that is a finding about YOUR OWN CAMPAIGN, and switching seeds discards it. An epidemic that depopulates shared surface/subterranean addresses on the canonical seed is exactly the sort of thing The Murrain should be reporting in its chronicle, not routing around in a test. If instead you switched for some other reason, say which.

   I cannot tell which from here, and you can: check whether seed 42 has any qualifying column at all now, and if it once did at 2103, what occ-ended / occ-ended-by say about it.

WHAT I WOULD SUBMIT: the search with the surface/subterranean condition added, the dead assert removed, the seed choice stated in the commit message with its reason, and -- if seed 42 did lose its shared columns to the plague -- a line in the chronicle saying so. I am not holding anything; your priority is live and the box is free whenever you push.
